facts.content: Patient has a left-sided throbbing headache since midday.
facts.source_text: CC: Left-sided throbbing HA since midday;

facts.content: The headache was preceded by a zig-zag visual aura and transient blurred vision.
facts.source_text: preceded by zig-zag visual aura & transient blurred vision

facts.content: The headache worsens with head or neck movement and is associated with photophobia and nausea/vomiting times two.
facts.source_text: Worse with head/neck movement; photophobia; N/V × 2

facts.content: There are no symptoms of fever, rash, speech disturbance, limb weakness, balance issues, head trauma, or shortness of breath.
facts.source_text: No fever, rash, speech disturbance, limb weakness, balance issues, head trauma, SOB

facts.content: A similar headache occurred a few weeks ago and lasted 2 days; otherwise, headaches are rare.
facts.source_text: Similar HA few wks ago, lasted 2 days; otherwise rare HAs

facts.content: Patient is concerned about having a brain tumor.
No past medical history is reported.
Patient has been taking Microgynon oral contraceptive pills for 3 months.
Patient works in the fashion industry with high stress and lives alone.
facts.source_text: Works in fashion industry, high stress; lives alone

facts.content: Patient is a non-smoker, does not consume alcohol, and has no exercise routine.
facts.source_text: non-smoker; no etOH; no exercise routine

facts.content: Diagnosis of migraine with aura, recurrent with typical features and no focal neurological signs.
facts.source_text: Migraine with aura – recurrent, typical features, no focal neuro signs

facts.content: Patient has health anxiety regarding intracranial malignancy.
Prescribed analgesia such as paracetamol or co-codamol, and NSAIDs like ibuprofen and naproxen as needed.
facts.source_text: Analgesia: paracetamol or co-codamol; NSAIDs (ibuprofen, naproxen) PRN

facts.content: Start a headache diary to track frequency and triggers.
facts.source_text: Start headache diary to track frequency/triggers

facts.content: Discuss prophylactic options if headaches increase and review next week.
facts.source_text: Discussed prophylactic options if HAs increase; review next week

facts.content: Safety net advice given to return if headache worsens or persists more than 2-3 days, or if there are new neurological deficits, vision changes, or increasing neck pain.
facts.source_text: Safety-net: return if HA worsens/persists >2-3 d, new neuro deficits, vision changes, increasing neck pain

facts.content: Provided reassurance about the low likelihood of a brain tumor.
